subject: Archaeology
title: The USS Indianapolis: A Tragic Discovery
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The USS Indianapolis: A Tragic Discovery.

hook.text: A U.S. cruiser was torpedoed in 1945 after delivering parts for the atomic bomb. 900 men went into the water.

buildup.text: The Navy did not notice the ship was missing for four days. Sailors drifted in shark-infested waters without lifeboats.

discovery.text: Only 316 of the 1,195 crew survived. It remains the worst single-ship loss in U.S. Navy history.

twist.text: The captain was court-martialed for the sinking. His record was not cleared until 2001, decades after his suicide.

climax.text: Paul Allen's research vessel found the wreck in 2017 at 18,000 feet — the ship was remarkably well preserved.

punchline.text: They delivered the bomb that ended a war. Nobody came to save them.

quiz.question: Why was the loss of the USS Indianapolis so devastating?
options: The ship was carrying thousands of civilian refugees
The Navy didn't notice it was missing for four days while survivors drifted
It was the largest warship ever sunk by a submarine

details.summary: The USS Indianapolis, sunk by a Japanese torpedo in 1945 after secretly delivering uranium for the Hiroshima bomb, was found in 2017 at 5,500 meters depth in the Philippine Sea. Only 316 of 1,196 crew survived, many killed by sharks while floating for days awaiting rescue.
details.whyItMatters: The Indianapolis discovery provided closure for survivors and families after 72 years. Finding the wreck at extreme depth demonstrated that modern technology can locate virtually any lost ship, no matter how deep.
takeaways: The Indianapolis was found in 2017 at 5,500 meters depth
Only 316 of 1,196 crew survived after the 1945 sinking
The discovery provided closure after 72 years for survivors

faq.question: Why did so many crew die after the sinking?
faq.answer: The ship sank in 12 minutes with no distress signal sent. Approximately 900 men entered the water alive, but the Navy didn't realize the ship was missing for nearly four days. Exposure, dehydration, salt poisoning, and shark attacks killed roughly 580 men before rescue arrived.

faq.question: How was the wreck finally found?
faq.answer: Paul Allen's research vessel R/V Petrel used advanced sonar and ROVs. New research into naval records pinpointed the ship's likely position more accurately than previous searches. The wreck was found sitting upright on the seafloor at 5,500 meters, one of the deepest wrecks documented.
